predecessors.name: Afsharid Iran
predecessors.text: Iran after Nader Shah, divided among warlords; the Afsharid line survived only in Khorasan under Shahrokh Shah

successors.name: Qajar dynasty
successors.text: Kerman and the south-east, taken in 1794; the Qajar already held the north

ledger.x: 1751: Karim Khan Zand holds Isfahan and founds the Zand regime.

c. 1752: the Zand realm grows from its Fars-Kerman core and Isfahan to the central and south-western provinces. Bridging event: the Zand Iran page says only that Karim Khan 'gained control of Iran's central and southern regions' and none of the pages opened (Karim Khan Zand, Azad Khan Afghan) dates a conquest of…
1753: Bahrain is held for the Zand by the Al Madhkur.
1760: Karim Khan holds all of Iran except Khorasan.
1760: the Caucasian khanates, de jure Zand.
1762: Shiraz becomes the Zand capital.
April 1775: the Zand besiege Basra.
April 1776: Basra surrenders.
April 1776: the Zand occupy Basra.
1778: Tehran becomes the second capital.
1779: the Zand leave Basra.
1779: Karim Khan dies and the khanates' Zand coinage and overlordship lapse.
2 April 1779: Agha Mohammad Khan defeats his brothers and conquers Mazandaran.

c. 1780: Zand rule over Azerbaijan lapses after Karim Khan's death. Bridging event: the Tabriz Khanate page has the Donboli pledging allegiance to Karim Khan in 1763, Najaf Qoli Khan made governor of Tabriz in 1769 and 'Zand's control over Azerbaijan unusually firm', but gives no date for its end; it has Sadiq Khan…

c. 1780: the Zand lose the western provinces after Karim Khan's death ('the country was under attack from all sides'). Bridging event: no page opened names who held Lorestan, Ilam or Khuzestan or when; the Cliopatria 1788 shape no longer holds them.

c. 1780: Sabzevar returns to Khorasan. Bridging event: the Zand Iran page excludes Khorasan 'except Sabzevar' but does not say when the Zand held or lost it; Cliopatria's 1788 shape no longer reaches it and Khorasan was ruled by Shahrokh Shah.
1781: the court moves to Isfahan (infobox 'Isfahan (1781-1785)').
1781: Agha Mohammad Khan seizes Qumis, Semnan, Damghan, Shahrud and Bastam.
1782: the Qajars invade Gilan.
1782: the Qajar take Qazvin and Zanjan.
28 July 1783: Bahrain leaves the Zand sphere.
1785: Tehran submits to the Qajar.
Summer 1785: Hamadan falls to the Qajar.
1785: the Qajar take the provinces between Tehran and Isfahan.
Summer 1785: the Kurdish chieftains submit to the Qajar.

c. 1785: Astarabad passes to the Qajar. Bridging event: the page has Morteza Qoli fortify Astarabad in 1779 and later 'serve the Zand dynasty', and Agha Mohammad retreat to Astarabad in 1784, but does not say when the Zand lost it; the Cliopatria 1788 shape no longer holds Golestan.
1785: the seat returns to Shiraz (infobox 'Shiraz (1785-1792)').
2 May 1785: the Qajar reach Isfahan.
Summer 1785: the Bakhtiari chieftains come under Qajar suzerainty.
1788: northern Yazd and Kohgiluyeh leave the Zand realm.
20 October 1788: the Zand retake Isfahan.
November 1788: the Zand lose Isfahan again.
1792: the Sheikh of Bushehr defects.
1792: the seat moves to Kerman (infobox 'Kerman (1792-1794)').
21 July 1792: Shiraz falls.
1794: the Qajar end the Zand.

wars.name: Siege of Basra (1775-1776)
wars.outcome: Zand victory: Basra surrendered on 20 April 1776 and was occupied until 1779, when the Zand withdrew after Karim Khan's death.

wars.name: Qajar conquest of the Zand dynasty
wars.outcome: Qajar victory: Agha Mohammad Khan took Mazandaran (1779), Semnan (1781), Gilan, Qazvin and Zanjan (1782), Tehran and Hamadan (1785), Isfahan (2 May 1785, held by the Zand 20 October to November 1788), Shiraz (21 July 1792) and Kerman (24 October 1794); Lotf…

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line fixes a Zand border: the eastern edge (Khorasan, Sistan) is approximate, the Caucasian khanates were 'de facto autonomous' and the Basra occupation of 1776-1779 had no agreed frontier.
